title: AIGP Practice Mock 2
description: IAPP AIGP-style mock: 100 scenario items. Exam-only timed practice; answers revealed after submit.

questions.question: A customer support platform deploys a generative AI assistant to draft responses for agents. After launch, the governance team sees a gradual rise in inaccurate answers for a newly released product line, even though performance on older products remains stable. The team suspects the model is relying on outdated patterns rather than current product information. Which governance action is MOST appropriate first?
options: Add live monitoring for drift indicators
Increase training epochs on old data
questions.rationale: The scenario points to performance degradation during live use for a specific, newly changed context, most consistent with drift or stale knowledge at inference. The best first response is to strengthen monitoring so the organization can detect, measure, and manage the issue before deciding on retraining or other remediation.
questions.topic: 10 - Data, Training, Testing, Inference, and Feedback Loops

questions.question: A financial services firm is retiring an older AI credit scoring system after replacing it with a newer model. The project manager proposes simply disabling the application and preserving all related data indefinitely in case questions arise later. What is the BEST governance response?
options: Delete all records to remove risk
Retire only after formal closure steps
Accept because future audits need data
questions.rationale: Retirement is a formal governance stage, not just shutting off a system. It includes handling data according to requirements, informing users, updating dependencies and records, and capturing lessons learned.

questions.question: A standardized documentation artifact accompanying an AI model at deployment that records intended use, known limitations, performance across subgroups, and ethical considerations is called a:
options: Model Card documenting intended use, limitations, subgroup performance, and ethical considerations
EU Declaration of Conformity attesting the system satisfies all high-risk AI requirements
Datasheet for Datasets recording why, how, and under what conditions training data was created
AI Policy Document stating binding organizational requirements for AI development and deployment governance
questions.rationale: A Model Card is the standardized documentation artifact accompanying an AI model at deployment, recording intended use, out-of-scope uses, training data summary, subgroup performance metrics, known limitations, and ethical considerations. It serves as an external communications artifact enabling deployers, users, and auditors to understand the model's design and limitations.

questions.question: A retailer’s customer-service chatbot sometimes gives incorrect store hours and, in rare cases, exposes private customer information. Security controls make the privacy incident unlikely, while wrong store hours occur regularly. If the governance lead is using a probability-severity matrix to decide where to focus executive attention, which risk should be flagged as MORE concerning?
options: Privacy exposure due to greater severity
Both equally due to customer impact
Wrong store hours due to higher frequency
questions.rationale: A probability-severity matrix distinguishes frequent low-impact issues from less likely but more damaging harms. Privacy exposure is a classic low-probability, high-severity risk.

questions.question: A DPO reviews the privacy policy before deploying an AI system that continuously analyzes employee productivity metrics. Which provision is MOST important to add under GDPR Article 13?
options: An explicit statement that automated profiling occurs, its logic, and employees' right to human review of significant decisions
A data minimization section specifying which essential performance metrics the AI may collect per employee role
A disclosure section listing all third-party vendors with authorized access to employee metrics reports from the AI system
A retention schedule specifying how long raw employee productivity metric data is stored before mandatory deletion
questions.rationale: GDPR Article 13(2)(f) requires proactive disclosure when automated decision-making including profiling occurs, its logic, and consequences. Deploying employee productivity AI without this disclosure in the privacy notice violates the transparency obligation before any data is processed.

questions.question: A global professional services firm wants to build trust in its internal AI assistant after employees express concern that the tool can access broad company information. Which leadership approach would BEST support responsible adoption?
questions.rationale: Responsible adoption depends on both formal direction and attention to the human side of trust, privacy, and control. Employees need support to understand how the tool works, what boundaries apply, and how to raise concerns.
questions.topic: 98 - Case Study Internal Generative AI Assistant

questions.question: A multinational health technology company is preparing to deploy the same AI triage tool in hospitals across Germany, several U.S. states, and China. The governance lead wants a single design principle that best reflects why the deployment plan cannot simply be copied across all three regions. Which principle is MOST important?
options: Cloud hosting location removes most regulatory differences
Technical model accuracy determines legal treatment everywhere
Regional AI rules shape design and operations differently
Open-source components reduce cross-border compliance burdens
questions.rationale: Regional AI regulation differs in structure, priorities, and implementation, which directly affects system design, deployment, workflows, and compliance strategy. Europe emphasizes stricter requirements; the United States relies more on sectoral and existing laws; China emphasizes alignment with government expectations and content controls.

questions.question: An HR team is preparing to procure a third-party AI screening platform. The vendor offers strong efficiency claims but refuses to explain training data sources, bias testing methods, or whether the model can be audited. What is the MOST appropriate governance response?
questions.rationale: Vendor review is a key governance control for AI used in sensitive contexts like hiring. If the organization cannot understand how the model was trained, tested, or audited, it cannot responsibly assess fairness, explainability, or compliance risk.
questions.topic: 94 - Case Study AI Resume Screening System

questions.question: An AI governance officer is aligning the organization's IP policy with the EU AI Act for a generative AI system that produces creative content. The current IP policy assigns copyright to the organization for employee works. Which gap must the updated policy address for AI-generated outputs?
options: Address uncertainty in copyright ownership of AI-generated content lacking human authorship
Classify all AI-generated text as public domain and waive organizational claims
Add a patent-pending notation to all AI-generated marketing materials before customer distribution
Require human co-authorship attestation for all AI-generated customer deliverables
questions.rationale: Existing IP policies built around human authorship do not address the legal ambiguity of AI-generated content. Most jurisdictions do not recognize AI as a copyright author, so the policy must explicitly address ownership claims, training data IP exposure, and how the organization will manage the resulting uncertainty.

questions.question: A law firm adopts an AI contract review system. It performs well, but the vendor refuses to share how the model was trained, what data was used, or which risks were assessed. Even internal staff don't know if the system meets legal compliance standards. Which AI property is most clearly lacking in this situation?
questions.rationale: Transparency involves openness about the design, training, data sources, and limitations of an AI system. Even if the tool works, refusing to disclose how it was built shows a clear transparency failure, not necessarily about individual predictions, but system-level clarity.

questions.question: An insurer wants to improve AI governance readiness without adding heavy manual work for underwriters. Which approach BEST balances compliance and operational efficiency?
questions.rationale: The best approach integrates compliance evidence collection into normal work so documentation is created as part of routine operations. This reduces burden while improving consistency and accessibility of records.

questions.question: A software company has an AI governance RACI that was created at project kickoff. Six months later, the team has added a third-party training dataset and a new cloud deployment model, but the RACI has not changed. What is the GREATEST governance weakness?
options: The team uses too few meetings
The model is no longer current
questions.rationale: AI projects evolve, and a RACI that is not updated fails to reflect new risks, vendors, or responsibilities. The RACI should be maintained as a living document.
questions.topic: 23 - AI Governance RACI and Stakeholder Accountability

questions.question: A logistics company proposes an AI system to reroute deliveries based on traffic and weather predictions. Senior leadership asks how the project’s value should be justified before approval. Which approach is BEST?
questions.rationale: Business justification should explain why the AI project is worth pursuing in concrete terms tied to organizational value. For a logistics use case, measurable benefits such as reduced delivery times, lower fuel costs, and improved customer satisfaction provide a sound basis.
questions.topic: 59 - AI Use Case Definition and Business Context

questions.question: A product team says its responsible design review is complete because the reviewers recorded several ethical risks in meeting minutes. No owners or deadlines were assigned. What is the GREATEST governance weakness?
questions.rationale: Responsible design reviews should not merely identify issues; they should assign follow-up actions and owners so risks are tracked and addressed. Without accountability, the review becomes a passive exercise rather than an effective control.
questions.topic: 63 - Ethics by Design and Responsible Design Reviews

questions.question: A healthcare organization’s imaging AI is highly accurate overall, but clinicians discover it often misses rare conditions affecting a small patient subgroup. Which governance action should have been emphasized EARLIEST in the project?
questions.rationale: The missed rare conditions represent a foreseeable harm affecting a specific group. Responsible AI governance requires identifying who may be negatively affected, documenting the risk, and planning mitigations before deployment.
questions.topic: 59 - AI Use Case Definition and Business Context

questions.question: A diagnostic AI model trained on general medical conditions is updated to focus on detecting rare tropical diseases. After the update, it starts failing to recognize common illnesses like flu or hypertension. What problem best describes this situation?
questions.rationale: This is a clear case of catastrophic forgetting, where the model learns a new task but loses previously acquired knowledge. The fine-tuning process focused heavily on rare tropical diseases without preserving earlier medical knowledge, causing performance on common conditions to degrade. Continual learning or rehearsal methods could help prevent this loss.

questions.question: A customer service team wants to train a new chatbot using archived support transcripts from five years ago, even though products and policies have changed substantially since then. Which governance concern should be raised FIRST?
questions.rationale: The main issue is whether the data is suitable for the intended purpose. Older transcripts may no longer reflect current products, policies, or customer issues, making them a poor basis for training a current chatbot.

questions.question: A Public Sector AI Policy team at a benefits agency is updating its acceptable use policy. The AI model recommends benefit denials, yet the policy has no human review requirement before notifications reach applicants. Which update BEST satisfies EU AI Act Article 14 and responsible AI accountability principles?
options: Require caseworkers to document rationale when overriding AI denial recommendations
Limit AI tool access to senior caseworkers with specific certification credentials
Require the AI vendor to log denial recommendations for quarterly audit review
Add a mandatory human review gate before any AI-recommended denial reaches applicants
questions.rationale: Benefits eligibility decisions fall within EU AI Act Annex III. Article 14 requires that high-risk AI systems allow natural persons to effectively monitor and intervene. A mandatory review gate before denial notifications are issued is the direct policy mechanism that satisfies both Article 14 and the accountability principle.

questions.question: A public-sector agency is preparing documentation for an AI service that will assist caseworkers. Regulators, internal audit, and frontline staff all need to understand the system’s purpose and limits. Which documentation approach is MOST effective?
options: Store technical notes within code comments
Limit access to senior data scientists
questions.rationale: Use case documentation should be clear, accessible, and usable by both technical and non-technical stakeholders. It should serve as a reference throughout the system lifecycle, supporting alignment, accountability, audits, and adaptation.
questions.topic: 59 - AI Use Case Definition and Business Context

questions.question: A healthcare provider is considering fine-tuning a pre-trained model using diagnostic notes that contain sensitive patient information. The data science team wants to use cloud resources because local infrastructure is limited. Which risk should the governance team analyze MOST carefully before approving the plan?
questions.rationale: Fine-tuning with sensitive data raises a key concern that the model may memorize and later reveal personal information, creating privacy and compliance exposure. While cloud capacity may be attractive, the review should focus on data exposure and legal risk.
questions.topic: 80 - Cloud, On-Premises, Edge, API, RAG, Fine-Tuning, and Ag

questions.question: A government department uses AI to prioritize citizen service requests. An internal review finds that the system is difficult to explain, and measurement tools are weak for assessing this emerging risk. Some executives want to continue unchanged because no legal complaint has been filed. Others want to stop all AI work indefinitely. Which is the BEST course of action?
options: Adapt controls, continue learning, and reassess regularly
Transfer explainability ownership to the procurement team
Suspend all AI initiatives until perfect tools exist
Maintain operations unchanged until formal complaints arise
questions.rationale: The framework recognizes that organizations may face limited tools for emerging risks such as explainability. The right response is to adapt, learn, collaborate, and reassess continuously. The RMF is a living process.
questions.topic: 53 - NIST AI Risk Management Framework Overview

questions.question: After a regulator finds that a company's fraud detection model was trained on unlawfully collected data, the company is ordered to remove not just the data, but all traces of its influence from their deployed model, without retraining from scratch. What is the enforcement mechanism being applied here?
questions.rationale: Model disgorgement is a regulatory action requiring the removal of all learned influence from unlawfully obtained data. It ensures that the model can no longer benefit from illegal data use, even if retraining is impractical.

questions.question: A ride-hailing app operating in China collects detailed location data and facial recognition images from users without proper consent. It also transfers this sensitive data to servers abroad. The Chinese authorities conduct an investigation and impose a hefty fine for violating national data protection regulations. Which law governs this situation?
questions.rationale: PIPL (China's Personal Information Protection Law) governs the handling of sensitive personal data in China. It mandates consent for biometric and location data and places restrictions on cross-border transfers. Other laws apply to the EU, Singapore/Thailand, or Brazil.

questions.question: A manufacturer is piloting AI-enabled robots in a warehouse. Tests show the system performs well in normal conditions, but error rates rise sharply during network disruptions and unusual lighting. Which governance conclusion is MOST appropriate?
questions.rationale: The OECD principle of robustness, security, and safety requires AI to function reliably under varied and difficult conditions, not just ideal ones. The system degrades during disruptions and unusual lighting, so robustness testing and resilience planning are not yet adequate.
questions.topic: 52 - OECD AI Principles and Trustworthy AI

questions.question: A lender uses a highly complex model that performs well, but regulators ask for reasons behind individual denials. The data science team argues that replacing the model would reduce predictive power. What is the BEST governance-oriented approach?
options: Shift denials to customer service staff
Use tools to explain influential features
questions.rationale: When complex models are needed, governance does not require abandoning them automatically. Explanation tools that identify the factors most influencing a decision support transparency and compliance.
questions.topic: 96 - Case Study Credit Scoring or Lending AI

questions.question: Which of the following is not typically included in the technical documentation required for a high-risk AI system under the EU AI Act?
options: Human oversight measures and their design
Description of potential harms or risks
questions.rationale: A DPIA is a separate requirement under the GDPR and not part of the AI Act’s technical documentation outlined in Annex IV. The AI Act focuses on elements like system architecture, risk identification, and human oversight to ensure transparency, accountability, and compliance for high-risk AI. While a DPIA might still be required under separate laws when personal data is involved, it is not part of the AI Act’s required documentation.

questions.question: A financial services firm launches an AI budgeting assistant that accurately follows its specifications, but its interface nudges users toward increasingly aggressive debt refinancing without meaningful guardrails for vulnerable customers. After complaints of avoidable financial harm, the AI governance committee asks which liability characterization is MOST defensible based on these facts. Which answer is BEST?
options: A warning label claim is weakest
A manufacturing defect claim is strongest
A design defect claim is strongest
questions.rationale: The system operates as intended, yet the intended design itself creates unreasonable risk by steering users toward harmful outcomes without safeguards. That aligns most closely with a design defect.
questions.topic: 51 - Product Liability and AI System Failure

questions.question: A retailer launches an AI customer analytics tool to predict shopping behavior. After strong early results, the business team begins using the tool to adjust individualized pricing and restrict access to certain promotions. What is the MOST appropriate governance response?
options: Keep current class until complaints rise
questions.rationale: AI risk classification is not fixed. When a system’s role expands into decisions that affect access or pricing, its impact on individuals becomes more serious. Reassess the use, update the classification if warranted, and adjust controls and documentation.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT included in the GDPR’s special categories of personal data?
questions.rationale: GDPR Article 9 defines special categories of personal data as those revealing racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious beliefs, trade union membership, genetic or biometric data, health data, or sex life and sexual orientation. Bank transaction history is personal data but not a special category under Article 9.

questions.question: A financial services firm wants a governance model that supports experimentation without allowing major risks to go unchecked. The chief innovation officer argues that every AI project should follow the same approval path to ensure consistency. Which approach is BEST?
options: Delegate all decisions to engineering leads
Approve pilots first and govern later
Use risk-tiered oversight by project impact
Apply identical reviews across all projects
questions.rationale: A risk-based approach allows high-risk projects to receive stronger scrutiny, while lower-risk experiments proceed with lighter oversight. This preserves agility without ignoring material harms.
questions.topic: 2 - How to Think Like an AI Governance Professional

questions.question: SmartSight GmbH, a German company, imports surveillance drones from a U.S.-based manufacturer, AeroVision Inc. These drones use AI-powered facial recognition and behavior analysis, making them high-risk AI systems under the EU AI Act. SmartSight GmbH must fulfill specific obligations before placing the systems on the EU market. Which of the following is NOT an obligation SmartSight GmbH must fulfill under the EU AI Act?
options: Prepare the technical documentation for the AI system
Keep records and documentation related to the AI system
Verify the CE marking and the declaration of conformity
Cooperate with competent authorities if requested
questions.rationale: Preparing the technical documentation is the responsibility of the provider (AeroVision Inc., in this case). As the importer, SmartSight GmbH must verify that the technical documentation exists, check for CE marking and conformity declaration, and retain documentation, but is not required to author the technical file.

questions.question: A healthcare organization is building an AI triage tool that uses patient information. During planning, legal says privacy controls are an IT matter, while IT says patient consent is a legal issue. Which risk is MOST likely if no RACI is established?
questions.rationale: When legal and IT each assume the other owns privacy responsibilities, sensitive data may be processed without proper consent or governance. Missing RACI assignments lead to ownership gaps with real legal consequences.
questions.topic: 23 - AI Governance RACI and Stakeholder Accountability

questions.question: An AI governance officer is conducting a gap analysis for a financial services firm adopting the NIST AI RMF. In a Private-Sector Compliance Program Design context, which output MOST directly enables production of a governance roadmap?
options: A list of deployed AI systems with residual risk scores and documented treatment decisions from the most recent assessment cycle
A crosswalk mapping existing policies to NIST AI RMF functions, categories, and subcategories showing current coverage
An AI RMF Profile selecting target outcome statements from the RMF Core aligned to the firm's risk posture
A prioritized list of missing controls, unclear accountabilities, and documentation gaps with owners and milestones
questions.rationale: The gap analysis produces a prioritized list of missing controls, accountability gaps, and documentation deficiencies; this list is the direct input from which a governance roadmap assigns owners, milestones, and resources to close identified gaps.

questions.question: During an AI Privacy Impact Assessment, a DPO identifies that the organization's existing data retention policy specifies a five-year maximum for customer records. An AI training dataset contains those same records. Which policy update is MOST appropriate to address the AI-specific retention issue?
options: Create a separate retention schedule for AI training datasets with documented justification and review triggers
Exempt AI training datasets from all retention requirements under a broad research exception covering model lifecycle stages
Apply the five-year ceiling uniformly to all AI training artifacts and derived model checkpoints without exception
Shorten AI training dataset retention to two years to be more conservative than the existing policy
questions.rationale: Existing retention policies for operational records fail to address AI training datasets, which embed personal data in model weights and have unique lifecycle needs. The correct approach is a separate, documented retention schedule that meets data minimization and purpose limitation principles while reflecting the actual lifecycle requirements of AI systems.

questions.question: In a Multi-Framework Alignment program, an AI governance officer needs to update the organization's supply chain policy to address AI model integrity risk. Which control BEST satisfies both NIST AI RMF MAP function requirements and EU AI Act Article 9?
options: Require pre-deployment model integrity testing including data poisoning detection before any vendor model enters production
Require all AI vendors to hold current ISO 42001 certification before contract execution as the primary integrity control
Require the vendor to provide contractual indemnification for losses caused by compromised or poisoned AI model outputs
Require quarterly penetration testing reports from the vendor covering all production AI inference infrastructure and endpoints
questions.rationale: NIST AI RMF MAP requires organizations to identify risks from third-party components before deployment. EU AI Act Article 9 mandates ongoing risk management including mitigation of foreseeable risks. Pre-deployment integrity testing that includes data poisoning detection satisfies both frameworks simultaneously.

questions.question: What is the PRIMARY purpose of a verified rollback procedure as a prerequisite for AI deployment authorization?
options: To document training data provenance before the model enters production and deployment authorization is granted
To enable rapid reversion to a prior validated AI version when the current deployment drifts or causes harm
To assign a named AI owner accountable for system decisions throughout its operational life
To record the AI system in the EU AI Act database before market placement and commercial deployment begins
questions.rationale: A verified rollback procedure is the pre-tested capability to revert a deployed AI system to a prior validated version when the current deployment fails, drifts, or causes harm. It is a mandatory deployment prerequisite: without a verified rollback path, an organization cannot rapidly deactivate or correct a harmful deployment.

questions.question: An AI ethics committee at an AI Ethics Committee Operations organization is reviewing a post-deployment monitoring report for a facial recognition access control system. The report shows stable accuracy but notes that adversarial spoofing attempts have increased 300% over the prior quarter. Which monitoring dimension MOST directly addresses this finding?
options: Bias monitoring tracking false acceptance rates across demographic groups using monthly sample audits
Security monitoring tracking adversarial attack patterns, spoofing attempt rates, and protective measure effectiveness
Performance drift monitoring comparing current recognition accuracy against the training distribution baseline
Data quality monitoring reviewing input image resolution and lighting conditions across access control locations
questions.rationale: A continuous monitoring program for AI systems must include a security monitoring dimension that tracks adversarial attack patterns, attempted exploits, and the effectiveness of protective measures. A 300% increase in spoofing attempts signals an active threat requiring immediate security response evaluation.

questions.question: Which of the following is least effective in reducing bias specifically during the planning phase?
options: Assessing the benefits of using AI versus not using AI
questions.rationale: Collecting representative data is essential for reducing bias but belongs to the design phase, not planning. Actions like setting governance, involving stakeholders, and questioning the AI need are all planning-phase interventions that shape the bias landscape early. Hence, this option is least relevant at this stage.

questions.question: A multinational organization operates AI systems in the EU and the US. The AI governance officer must update the organization's data governance policy to address cross-border data transfers used in AI model training. Which provision is MOST critical to add to the policy for EU-to-US data flows?
options: A clause requiring model training to use only synthetic data generated within the EU under approved generation methodologies
A clause requiring valid transfer mechanisms such as adequacy decisions or SCCs for all EU-origin personal data used in AI training
A clause requiring data subjects to consent in writing to AI model training before any personal data is used in pipelines
A clause requiring all AI training data to be stored only within EU data centers under certified hosting providers
questions.rationale: GDPR Chapter V prohibits transfers of personal data to third countries without a valid mechanism like an adequacy decision or Standard Contractual Clauses. This applies when EU personal data is transferred to US-based AI training infrastructure.

questions.question: A retailer is piloting an AI capability to classify product images for its online catalog. The data science team says the model is highly accurate in testing, but operations leaders say it still cannot be used in production. Which concern BEST explains why a strong model alone is insufficient?
questions.rationale: This tests the distinction between an AI model and an AI system. A model becomes useful in practice only when embedded in an environment that connects it to data, workflows, rules, monitoring, and user interaction.
questions.topic: 9 - AI Models, AI Systems, and AI Products

questions.question: A transportation company suffered a major outage in an AI-assisted dispatch platform after an untested edge case. Executives want the response to reduce repeat failures over time rather than only restore service quickly. Which action is MOST appropriate after recovery?
options: Increase customer messaging until complaints decline
Conduct root-cause analysis and share lessons learned
Freeze all model changes pending budget approval
Replace dashboards with manual status emails
questions.rationale: Long-term improvement comes from learning systematically from failure. A post-mortem or root-cause analysis identifies what happened, why it happened, and how to prevent recurrence. Sharing lessons also strengthens organizational resilience.

questions.question: A multinational firm's AI acceptable use policy prohibits employees from entering client confidential information into external AI tools. A business unit in Germany begins using an external AI assistant for contract summarization and inputting client data. Which element of deploying the acceptable use policy MOST directly prevents this violation going forward?
options: Role-based training modules explaining why client data entry into external AI tools is prohibited
Technical access controls blocking external AI service domains from the corporate network
A policy attestation form requiring the German business unit to acknowledge the acceptable use policy
An exception process allowing the business unit to request approved use of external AI tools for specific workflows
questions.rationale: When an AI acceptable use policy is violated, governance must include technical controls to prevent prohibited behavior, not just rely on policy awareness. Network-level access controls that block external AI service domains turn the policy prohibition into a technical constraint that employees cannot bypass from corporate infrastructure.

questions.question: A multinational company has implemented bias testing, diverse training data, and decision transparency for an internal promotion model. An executive asks whether the company can now state that the fairness risk has been eliminated. What is the BEST response from the AI governance lead?
questions.rationale: Even strong controls do not reduce AI risk to zero. Residual risk remains after treatment, and governance should acknowledge that reality while continuing monitoring and review.

questions.question: A mature enterprise is redesigning its AI data lifecycle program after criticism that deletion requests are handled inconsistently. Which investment would provide the GREATEST overall improvement?
questions.rationale: The broadest improvement comes from strengthening operational control across the lifecycle through automated tracking of data locations and dependencies, supported by auditability. This addresses inconsistency, hidden copies, downstream uses, and accountability.
questions.topic: 71 - Data Retention, Deletion, and Model Dependencies

questions.question: An AI governance committee is reviewing a proposal to use several external datasets in a generative AI project. Documentation is inconsistent: one team has consent records, another has only emails, and a third cannot explain where its data originated. Which action should the committee prioritize?
questions.rationale: A core principle of lawful data use is knowing the source of data, the permissions attached to it, and any restrictions on use. If a team cannot explain where data came from, the organization cannot be confident it has the right to use it. Stop use of undocumented datasets until rights are established and recorded.

questions.question: A regional hospital deploys an AI tool to prioritize radiology cases. The CIO reports that the platform is encrypted, highly available, and fully patched. Several physicians still object that the organization has not yet established adequate governance. Which concern BEST justifies their position?
options: The model may miss rare cases
questions.rationale: AI governance goes beyond traditional IT controls such as uptime, patching, and encryption. A model that misses rare cases creates patient safety, fairness, and accountability concerns that standard IT governance does not fully address.

questions.question: A fraud detection team reports that suspicious transactions are bypassing its AI model after attackers made tiny changes to transaction details that appear normal to analysts. Which AI weakness does this MOST strongly indicate?
questions.rationale: Small, hard-to-notice changes causing misclassification of malicious activity are characteristic of adversarial examples, where crafted inputs fool the model while appearing normal to humans.
questions.topic: 16 - Privacy, Security, and Data Protection in AI

questions.question: A consumer platform’s chatbot begins generating offensive responses. The engineering team proposes adding a quick output blocklist and moving on, while the governance team argues for a deeper review. Which approach is BEST?
questions.rationale: The best approach is to investigate the underlying cause rather than only masking the symptom. Lasting corrective action requires understanding and addressing the true cause.
questions.topic: 90 - AI Issue Management and Corrective Actions

questions.question: A hospital is implementing an AI model to predict which patients are at elevated risk of readmission. The model will use identifiable patient records and produce recommendations for care teams. Which legal concern should the AI governance team prioritize FIRST when designing controls?
questions.rationale: Because the system uses identifiable patient records, the first governance priority is privacy law and the handling of personal information. Other legal issues may arise later, but the immediate and most direct concern is lawful and secure use of patient data.
questions.topic: 37 - How Laws Apply to AI Systems

questions.question: A global retailer receives a customer request to see all personal data held across marketing, support, loyalty, and fraud systems. Each team maintains separate tools and no one can quickly identify all records. Which improvement would MOST directly strengthen future response capability?
questions.rationale: When data is fragmented across many systems, the most direct way to improve access request handling is to map where data resides and how it moves. Data flow mapping supports discovery, coordination, and timely responses.
questions.topic: 45 - Data Subject Rights and Automated Decision-Making

questions.question: A social media platform uses AI moderation. Leaders want to reduce all moderation mistakes, but engineers warn that adding every possible review step would make the service too slow for users. Which response BEST reflects sound AI governance?
questions.rationale: Effective AI risk management requires weighing benefits and costs. If excessive controls would make the system unusable, balance risk reduction with operational practicality, often through a mix of controls.

questions.question: A global firm is integrating third-party datasets, open-source libraries, and vendor components into a new AI service. Senior management wants the MOST effective governance action to reduce the risk of hidden malicious code or poisoned data entering through trusted dependencies. What should be prioritized?
questions.rationale: Supply chain risk is best addressed through disciplined governance over third-party code and datasets, including vetting, maintaining an inventory, scanning for vulnerabilities, and monitoring for suspicious changes.
questions.topic: 75 - AI Security Testing and Threat Modeling

questions.question: A bank discovers that its AI loan screening tool has rejected nearly all applications from one geographic region for two days. An executive wants the team to simply adjust the threshold and resume operations. What is the MOST appropriate next step for the issue owner?
questions.rationale: Adjusting a symptom without understanding the cause risks recurrence and may hide deeper failures. Root cause analysis looks beyond the symptom to determine whether the issue arose from algorithm changes, missing fields, data pipeline failures, or external provider changes.
questions.topic: 90 - AI Issue Management and Corrective Actions

questions.question: A large retailer experiences a public incident after attackers manipulate its chatbot into producing offensive responses on social media screenshots. The security team wants to focus only on blocking the exploit path, while communications leaders warn of broader consequences. Which statement BEST reflects sound AI governance?
options: Both technical and organizational measures matter
questions.rationale: Chatbot incidents create both technical and reputational risks. Governance must include organizational response, testing, communication, and continuous improvement alongside technical controls.

questions.question: An AI ethics committee is designing a supply chain risk policy for AI components. The organization integrates open-source foundation models from community repositories. Which risk is PRIMARY to address in the policy's supply chain provisions?
options: The risk that using open-source models will expose the organization to software licensing compliance violations
The risk that open-source model weights contain data poisoning from community-contributed modifications
The risk that open-source models will underperform proprietary alternatives on accuracy benchmarks
The risk that open-source models will be deprecated and become unsupported by their community
questions.rationale: The main supply chain risk for open-source foundation models is data poisoning from community-contributed modifications. Deploying open-source models means the organization assumes full responsibility for safety evaluation due to the absence of provider-side controls.

questions.question: Under ISO 42001, which document records the organization's rationale for including or excluding each Annex A control from its AI management system?
options: The Statement of Applicability, documenting Annex A control selections and exclusion rationale
The AIMS Scope Statement, which defines the management system boundary and exclusions
The Risk Register, cataloging AI risks with treatment decisions and residual levels
The AI Policy, which states the organization's strategic AIMS commitments and direction
questions.rationale: ISO 42001 requires organizations to select relevant Annex A controls and document their applicability decisions, including rationale for any controls excluded. The Statement of Applicability fulfills this requirement and is a primary audit artifact.

questions.question: A consumer speech-recognition system designed for home assistants is adopted by a court clerk's office to transcribe testimony. Which factor BEST explains why this creates new governance risk even if the system performs as designed?
questions.rationale: A system can function exactly as designed and still create serious governance issues when used in a new setting. Moving a consumer tool into a courtroom changes the stakes, user expectations, and legal implications. Context, not just technical function, determines risk.
questions.topic: 86 - Secondary Use, Unintended Use, and Downstream Harm

questions.question: A healthcare AI chatbot originally collected only symptom descriptions, but a product update now proposes collecting users’ genetic information and location data to improve recommendations. What should the AI governance team do FIRST to manage this change appropriately?
questions.rationale: When an AI system changes to collect new sensitive data, the first governance step is to identify and map where that data is collected, processed, and stored. Updated data flow mapping supports later decisions about controls, notices, retention, and escalation.
questions.topic: 46 - Sensitive Data, Biometrics, and Special Categories

questions.question: A regulator is considering how to oversee AI used in hiring, medical devices, and customer chatbots. The policy team wants stronger controls where harms could be greatest while avoiding unnecessary burdens on low-impact tools. Which approach BEST matches that objective?
options: Uniform controls for all AI systems
questions.rationale: A risk-based model aligns regulatory burden with potential harm. High-risk uses such as hiring and medical devices receive stricter transparency, oversight, and control requirements, while lower-risk tools face lighter obligations.

questions.question: A rail operator uses an automated control system that handles routine speed and braking decisions. An operator continuously monitors the system and may intervene if it behaves unexpectedly, but does not approve each routine action. Which oversight model BEST describes this arrangement?
questions.rationale: Human-on-the-loop applies when a person supervises system operation and can intervene when necessary, without participating in every individual decision.

questions.question: A company acquires an external machine learning model for customer support automation. During due diligence, the AI governance lead learns the model was trained on poorly curated data, but the vendor insists performance metrics are acceptable. What is the BEST governance decision before deployment?
questions.rationale: This is a classic third-party risk: the organization may inherit hidden weaknesses from a vendor model. The best decision is to strengthen vendor vetting and establish ongoing monitoring before deployment.

questions.question: During an AI governance review, internal auditors discover that a credit scoring model has not been updated to reflect newer privacy requirements. Management asks the auditors to redesign the process and approve the remediation plan before implementation. What should the auditors do NEXT?
questions.rationale: Internal audit provides independent assurance by identifying weaknesses, recommending improvements, and following up on remediation. Auditors should avoid taking ownership of operational fixes or approvals because that would impair independence.

questions.question: An AI governance officer is conducting a secondary-use risk forecast as part of an ISO 42001 Clause 8 AI system impact assessment. Which forecast methodology is MOST aligned with the impact assessment requirement?
options: Commission an independent external ethics audit to identify secondary misuse scenarios the internal team may have overlooked in the ISO Clause 8 impact assessment
Review historical misuse patterns from comparable deployed AI tools and map plausible secondary uses to affected stakeholder groups and potential consequences
Conduct a NIST AI RMF MAP categorization of all current authorized primary use cases to confirm completeness of the documented use-case inventory before assessing secondary uses
Survey business unit leaders on their planned uses of the AI system over the next fiscal year to surface anticipated secondary applications before they materialize
questions.rationale: ISO 42001 Clause 8 requires a structured AI system impact assessment evaluating potential consequences for all affected stakeholder groups. For secondary-use risk forecasting, the appropriate methodology is reviewing historical misuse patterns from comparable tools, identifying plausible secondary uses, and mapping them to affected groups with consequence estimates.

questions.question: A software company offers API access to a proprietary AI model. Security analysts notice a competitor sending large volumes of systematic test queries designed to infer how the model behaves under many conditions. Which control would BEST address this risk?
questions.rationale: The scenario points to model extraction through repeated interaction intended to reconstruct the model. Limiting and randomizing queries makes systematic reconstruction more difficult.
questions.topic: 75 - AI Security Testing and Threat Modeling

questions.question: Under the EU AI Act, which role describes an entity that places an AI system on the market under its own name?
options: Deployer who integrates AI into internal business workflows
Provider who develops or markets AI under its own branding
Distributor who makes systems available in the supply chain
Importer who brings systems from third-country providers into the EU
questions.rationale: The EU AI Act defines a provider as any entity that places an AI system on the market or into service under its own name. This distinguishes providers from deployers, importers, and distributors. Providers handle the highest compliance burden, including conformity assessments for high-risk AI.

questions.question: A mature enterprise uses a GRC platform to automate control mapping, evidence tracking, and reporting for its AI governance program. The chief risk officer wants to rely on the platform to resolve conflicts between legal, security, and ethics requirements. What is the BEST response from the program lead?
questions.rationale: Technology can streamline governance tasks, but it cannot replace expert interpretation, cross-functional collaboration, and judgment. Conflicts between legal, security, and ethical requirements require human analysis and decision-making.
questions.topic: 58 - Mapping Standards to One Governance Program

questions.question: An e-commerce company uses an AI model to rank customer support tickets. The model is accurate in testing, but complaints show that tickets from certain customer groups are consistently deprioritized. Which additional testing category would MOST directly address this issue?
questions.rationale: When outcomes systematically disadvantage certain groups, the most direct response is bias or fairness testing. Testing strategies should map test types to the specific risk presented.

questions.question: A retail company deploys an AI agent to monitor inventory, place replenishment orders, and update accounting records without waiting for human approval. Which characteristic MOST clearly makes this system agentic rather than merely assistive?
questions.rationale: The defining feature of agentic AI here is that it does not stop at analysis or recommendation; it takes action across business systems to complete work. Executing orders and updating accounting records are end-to-end operational actions.
questions.topic: 99 - Case Study Agentic AI Workflow Automation

questions.question: Which incident management step assigns a category and severity tier to determine notification obligations?
options: Containment, which restricts the scope of active harm to affected system components
Incident classification, which drives response and notification requirements
Evidence preservation, which secures artifacts for investigation
Regulatory notification, which informs supervisory authorities of harm
questions.rationale: Classification assigns category and severity tier first; those assignments determine which containment pathway activates and which regulatory timelines apply. Skipping or deferring classification leaves notification obligations undefined.

questions.question: Which periodic assessment activity produces a prioritized register of attack vectors and recommended controls for an AI system?
options: Compliance audit verifying adherence to documented governance requirements
Threat modeling enumerating attack surfaces and recommending mitigating controls
Bias audit evaluating disparate impact across protected demographic groups
Red-team exercise simulating adversarial scenarios to probe system failures
questions.rationale: Threat modeling is the structured methodology for enumerating an AI system's attack surface and producing a prioritized register of attack vectors with recommended controls. Red-teaming then tests those identified vectors, but the register itself is the output of threat modeling.

questions.question: An insurer uses a third-party cloud AI service to automate claims triage. The vendor suffers an outage during a storm event, delaying thousands of claims. The AI governance committee wants the taxonomy to guide the FIRST mitigation improvement. Which action BEST aligns the identified risk?
questions.rationale: The scenario is primarily about third-party and operational risk. The best first mitigation is to strengthen contractual protections and service commitments. The other options address ethics, reputational response, and legal review.

questions.question: A clinic deploys an AI chatbot to answer patient questions. After rollout, the impact assessment record shows the chatbot handles routine inquiries well but sometimes misinterprets urgent symptoms. The clinic wants a mitigation that BEST aligns with responsible AI use. What should it do?
questions.rationale: When an AI system performs adequately in common cases but creates safety concerns in higher-risk situations, add targeted controls that reduce harm while preserving value. Routing unclear or urgent cases to human staff is a proportionate mitigation.

questions.question: A financial services firm is redesigning its chatbot governance program after several minor issues involving inaccurate answers, weak handoffs, and inconsistent customer messaging about AI use. Leadership asks for the MOST effective overall approach. Which option is BEST?
options: Shift all risk to the vendor
questions.rationale: Responsible chatbot governance requires an integrated approach. The issues span accuracy, escalation, and transparency, so the best response combines design safeguards, clear disclosure, and continuous monitoring.

questions.question: A consumer health company wants to build trust in a symptom triage model after a widely publicized AI failure in the industry. Leadership asks what documentation practice would MOST strengthen informed decision-making by users and stakeholders. Which recommendation is BEST?
questions.rationale: Trust is strengthened when users and stakeholders can understand what a model is for, how it performs, where it may fail, and what risks or limitations apply. Clear documentation supports informed use, accountability, and safer deployment.
questions.topic: 77 - Model Cards, Data Sheets, and Technical Documentation

questions.question: A company completed a rapid integration of its AI, security, and privacy governance requirements. During an internal audit, reviewers discover that explicit consent obligations for certain data uses were omitted because the team assumed general security controls covered them. What is the MOST important lesson for the governance lead?
options: Security teams should own all compliance
General controls usually satisfy privacy law
questions.rationale: Rushed integration can miss unique obligations unless the mapping is detailed and reviewed by appropriate experts. General controls do not automatically satisfy distinct legal requirements.
questions.topic: 58 - Mapping Standards to One Governance Program

questions.question: A technology company faces changing guidance on acceptable controls for an internal AI monitoring process. The requirements are not fully clear, and the team has adjusted procedures several times. Which action would MOST reduce enforcement risk in this situation?
questions.rationale: When requirements are unclear or evolving, defensible documentation of the organization’s interpretation, actions, and any regulator guidance helps demonstrate reasonable, good-faith compliance efforts.

questions.question: A smart gardening robot causes damage. It uses embedded AI for navigation, a real-time weather data service for movement, a 3D printing design file for parts, and a user-installed open-source monitoring app. Under the revised EU Product Liability Directive, which of the following elements is NOT in scope for liability?
options: The monitoring app installed by the user
The digital manufacturing file used to 3D-print a component of the robot
The real-time weather data service used for decision-making
The embedded AI software controlling the robot's navigation
questions.rationale: The directive applies to software, digital services, and files integral to a product's function. However, a user-installed, community-developed app provided outside of commercial activity is excluded and thus not within the directive’s liability scope.

questions.question: A regulator asks a company to show how its AI hiring tool avoids bias and how staff were prepared to use it responsibly. The program lead has model code, but little else. Which missing evidence would be MOST important to demonstrate governance across gates?
questions.rationale: Governance evidence should show that gates were followed and responsibilities were met. For a hiring tool, the most relevant proof includes design documentation addressing bias concerns and user training logs showing operational readiness.

questions.question: An internal audit of AI governance finds that product teams are highly creative and motivated, but they rarely share practices, use different standards, and cannot easily demonstrate compliance across the enterprise. Which recommendation is BEST?
questions.rationale: The findings point to federated governance risks: silos, inconsistent standards, and difficulty proving compliance. Cross-team forums and shared training improve alignment without destroying the benefits of local ownership.

questions.question: In which of the following activities are government regulators or policy advisors typically not involved?
options: Approval, certification, or registration of high-risk AI systems
questions.rationale: Red teaming and adversarial testing are usually internal or third-party exercises driven by developers or auditors. While government regulators may encourage robustness, they don’t directly create or manage red team testbeds. In contrast, regulators are formally involved in oversight, approval, and enforcement tasks, especially under AI laws like the EU AI Act or sector-specific compliance regimes.

questions.question: An AI governance officer at a Private-Sector Compliance Program Design company is conducting a pre-deployment review. The stage gate requires evidence of deployment authorization before go-live. Which element MOST directly constitutes formal deployment authorization under AIGP governance standards?
options: The data science team lead's email confirming model accuracy exceeds the required threshold
The AI owner's documented sign-off confirming acceptance criteria are met and the system may proceed
The security team's penetration test report confirming no critical vulnerabilities in the inference endpoint
The model card published to the production documentation portal indicating readiness for use
questions.rationale: Formal deployment authorization is the AI owner's documented sign-off at a stage gate confirming that all acceptance criteria are met, required controls are in place, and the system is cleared for production. Informal communications, technical reports, and ancillary artifacts like model cards serve as inputs or accompaniments to the authorization decision, not the authorization itself.

questions.question: An AI risk officer at an insurance company finds the data governance policy has no provision for AI training data provenance. Which control is MOST important to add to the policy standard?
options: A mandatory data provenance record documenting source, lawful basis, and authorized use for each training dataset
A requirement to document commercial data vendor contracts, license terms, and renewal dates for AI training datasets
A prohibition on synthetic data in training pipelines without model validation committee approval
A requirement that all AI training datasets undergo statistical quality scoring before pipeline ingestion
questions.rationale: Provenance documentation establishes whether training data was collected lawfully and used within its authorized scope. Insurance AI systems processing policyholder data face GDPR purpose limitation and lawful basis obligations that cannot be demonstrated without a provenance record per dataset.

questions.question: A company’s AI governance lead is told that fairness concerns should be handled entirely by the machine learning team because “this is a technical bug problem.” Which response is BEST?
options: Fairness belongs only to legal counsel
Fairness should wait for production metrics
Fairness requires rules, oversight, and explanation
Fairness depends only on coding quality
questions.rationale: Bias and fairness are governance issues as well as technical issues. Effective management requires processes, oversight, monitoring, and communication with affected people.
questions.topic: 14 - Fairness and Bias in AI Governance

questions.question: A consumer lender wants to launch an AI underwriting system quickly because competitors are advertising AI-driven approvals. The proposed use case remains vague, and new features are being added weekly. What should the AI governance lead recommend?
questions.rationale: This situation combines two classic governance risks: pressure to build because AI is popular and scope creep that blurs the original purpose. Pause and revisit the use case definition to clarify objectives, users, harms, and boundaries before proceeding.
questions.topic: 59 - AI Use Case Definition and Business Context

questions.question: A regulator asks an insurer to demonstrate that its underwriting model can be maintained, reproduced, and safely updated over time. The insurer can provide a concise summary of purpose and risks, plus a detailed dataset description. What additional documentation is MOST necessary?
questions.rationale: The regulator’s request focuses on reproducibility, maintenance, and safe updates. Technical documentation includes code versions, hyperparameters, procedures, infrastructure requirements, monitoring, retraining, and update workflows.
questions.topic: 77 - Model Cards, Data Sheets, and Technical Documentation

questions.question: Which structural requirement distinguishes the AI Risk Officer role from first-line AI governance roles?
options: The role must hold a recognized AI governance certification.
The role must own the risk register and manage all exception decisions
The role must report directly to the board rather than to management
The role must be independent from first-line AI build-and-operate teams
questions.rationale: The AI Risk Officer is the second-line oversight function; structural independence from first-line AI teams is the design requirement that makes the role's risk assessments credible and prevents capture by the teams being overseen.

questions.question: A technology firm is revising its AI governance program after several projects treated testing as a final-stage checklist. The chief AI officer wants a change that will most improve long-term reliability and stakeholder confidence. Which action is BEST?
questions.rationale: Mature AI governance treats testing as part of organizational culture rather than an afterthought. Embedding testing throughout development and openly sharing results supports continuous improvement, stronger assurance, and stakeholder trust.

questions.question: An organization has all major AI governance roles formally assigned, yet incidents still reveal confusion during model failures and data leak scenarios. Leaders want a practical way to strengthen coordination, expose gaps, and improve shared response capability across teams. Which step is BEST?
questions.rationale: When roles exist but coordination remains weak, practical rehearsals are highly effective. Tabletop exercises bring stakeholders together to walk through incidents, clarify escalation paths, reveal blind spots, and strengthen working relationships.

questions.question: A company’s AI recruitment tool automatically rejects applicants below a model-generated threshold. During an internal review, the compliance lead learns there is no documented appeal path for rejected candidates. Which gap is MOST significant?
questions.rationale: In a high-risk employment context, organizations should provide a way for affected individuals to challenge decisions. An automated rejection process without review or appeal is a major governance and compliance gap.

questions.question: A manufacturer deploys AI in a medical diagnostic device. After a missed condition leads to patient harm, executives ask who should be considered responsible. Which response BEST reflects sound AI governance judgment?
options: Liability never applies to AI errors
The user alone is always liable
Responsibility is shared and records matter
The developer alone is always liable
questions.rationale: Liability for AI-caused harm is often complex and depends on jurisdiction, use case, and legal theory. Responsibility may be shared among producers, developers, deployers, and users, and organizations should maintain safety checks, guidance, and records.
questions.topic: 37 - How Laws Apply to AI Systems

questions.question: A regional hospital is evaluating two external AI vendors for medical image triage. Vendor A shows strong demo accuracy but will not explain its training data or decision logic. Vendor B shows slightly lower demo accuracy but provides detailed documentation on methodology, data sources, and security controls. Which factor should MOST influence the hospital’s selection from an AI governance perspective?
questions.rationale: Vendor selection is not only about headline performance. The hospital must be able to understand, assess, and stand behind the system it deploys. Transparency supports risk assessment, trust, accountability, and informed oversight.
questions.topic: 81 - Vendor AI and Third-Party Model Selection

questions.question: A utility company deploys an AI system to optimize electricity distribution across several regions. After two weeks, operators report that the system improves efficiency but occasionally recommends actions that increase outage risk during peak demand. The vendor says the behavior is within expected tolerances and offers a future model update. Regulators have asked how the company is governing live use of the system. What is the BEST immediate action for the AI governance lead?
options: Shift monitoring to the vendor since the issue appears model-specific
Accept the current risk because the efficiency gains remain significant overall
Keep the system active, but require operator override for high-risk recommendations
Pause all AI use until the vendor delivers a corrected model version
questions.rationale: The best immediate action keeps operations controlled while reducing harm exposure through human oversight on high-risk recommendations. This is more proportionate than a full shutdown and more accountable than deferring responsibility to the vendor or tolerating known risk.
questions.topic: 103 - Domain IV Review — Governing AI Deployment and Use

questions.question: A DPO conducting a DPIA for a new AI profiling system finds the privacy policy has no lawful basis statement for AI-powered behavioral profiling of website visitors. Under GDPR, which update is MOST important before deployment?
options: Add a retention schedule for behavioral profile data collected over a twelve-month period
Document a valid GDPR Article 6 lawful basis, with a legitimate interests balancing test if applicable
Add a right to data portability for behavioral profile data per GDPR Article 20 enabling subjects to request profiles
Conduct a separate DPIA citing Article 35 systematic profiling as the trigger condition
questions.rationale: GDPR Article 6 requires every processing activity to have a valid lawful basis before it begins. An AI profiling system cannot be deployed lawfully without this in the privacy policy. If relying on legitimate interests, a balancing test must also be documented. All other privacy controls depend on this foundational authorization step.

questions.question: A large corporation deploys an AI-based resume screening system that disproportionately filters out Black candidates. Historical bias is embedded in the training data. Which law is LEAST likely to apply in this case?
options: Title VII of the Civil Rights Act
questions.rationale: Title VII prohibits employment discrimination by race; FCRA may apply if external screening reports are used; the FTC Act applies to unfair/deceptive practices. ECOA is least applicable since it applies to credit, not employment.

questions.question: A media platform wants to launch an AI feature that generates and edits short videos for users in China. During review, legal counsel highlights obligations tied to deep synthesis technologies. Which product change is MOST directly responsive?
options: Add clear labels to AI-generated media
Shift model training to foreign servers
questions.rationale: China’s deep synthesis rules emphasize clear labeling of AI-generated or altered media and mechanisms to prevent misuse. For a media platform, labeling is a direct and concrete response to that regulatory expectation.

questions.question: A healthcare provider is reviewing an AI diagnostic support tool used by physicians. The vendor proposes full automation for routine cases to improve throughput. Which control would BEST align with responsible impact assessment for this use case?
options: Restrict use to historical patient records
Require doctors to retain final decision authority
questions.rationale: In high-risk contexts such as healthcare, human oversight is essential. AI should function as a guide rather than a replacement for accountable decision-makers. The strongest control is to ensure clinicians retain authority and can review or override AI recommendations.

questions.question: A software company is preparing to launch an AI feature built partly on code and model components obtained from several vendors. During final review, legal counsel warns that unauthorized use of third-party materials could create significant exposure. Which risk area is MOST directly implicated?
questions.rationale: When a company uses software, code, or other protected materials without proper authorization, the primary issue is intellectual property infringement.
questions.topic: 101 - Domain II Review — Laws, Standards, and Frameworks

questions.question: A retail store installs facial recognition cameras that try to guess whether customers are religious or support a particular political party. Based on this guess, the system shows different ads or offers different discounts. What risk category does this use case fall under under the EU AI Act?
options: Outside the scope of the Act
questions.rationale: This use case involves using biometric systems to infer sensitive attributes like religion or political opinion in real time for behavioral manipulation. This is explicitly banned under Article 5 of the EU AI Act.

questions.question: A clinic’s AI triage tool was introduced to reduce review time. After six months, physicians report that it recommends too many unnecessary follow-up tests, increasing costs and patient anxiety. What is the BEST next step?
options: Compare outcomes to original use case
questions.rationale: When post-deployment issues emerge, return to the original use case definition and assess whether the system is meeting its intended goals within acceptable risk boundaries.
questions.topic: 59 - AI Use Case Definition and Business Context

questions.question: A university runs an online entrance exam platform and keeps students’ webcam footage and screen recordings for over five years, even though all results were finalized within three months. Which data protection principle is most relevant here?
questions.rationale: Storage limitation means personal data should be retained only for as long as necessary. Keeping surveillance footage for years after results are out is disproportionate and increases privacy risks.
